name: Contemporary craft product
region: Belgium, Japan, Scandinavia, Britain and the United States
summary: The handmade object of the quiet home: stoneware with a speckled glaze, solid oak with an oiled finish, washed linen and unlacquered brass, made in small batches and left with the marks of the hand.

philosophy.core_thesis: A good object is made by a person from one real material, and it gains value with use: its marks, its tone and its slow wear are the ornament.
design_principles: Use a solid material, not a veneer: oak 25 to 50 mm thick, stoneware with a wall of 5 to 8 mm.
Finish with oil, soap, wax or a matte glaze; keep the gloss below 15 GU.
Leave one mark of the maker on each object: a throwing ring, a plane mark or a hammer facet.
Make each form from a simple shape with slightly uneven edges and a soft radius of 3 to 10 mm.
Keep to a palette of 4 or 5 warm neutrals: oat, sand, clay, bone and a soft black.
Use brass without lacquer, so that it darkens with the hand and the years.
Make in batches of 1 to 100 pieces and sign the base or the back.
anti_patterns: Logos and visible fixings on main faces

form.geometry: The cylinder, the squat jar, the slab and the plain box, with slightly uneven edges and soft volumes.
form.silhouette: A calm, low and broad outline with a heavy base and a small, quiet detail on top.
form.edges: Soft radius of 3 to 10 mm on wood; a pulled lip and an uneven rim on a vessel; a chamfer of 2 mm on a slab.
form.proportion: A table top is 30 to 45 mm thick; a vase is 20 to 35 cm high with a wall of 5 to 8 mm; a low sofa seat is 38 cm high.
form.ornament: None applied. The grain, the glaze, the throwing rings and the weave are the only surface pattern.
rules: Each object uses 1 to 3 natural materials in view.
Each object shows at least 1 mark of the hand or the tool.
A vessel has a wall of 5 mm or more and a visible foot.
A surface has no gloss above 15 GU, except a brass part.
A colour other than the colour of the material covers less than 10% of the object.

materials.rule: Wood, clay, stone and cloth make about 85% of the visible surface; brass is the one metal.

finish.gloss: 2–12 GU on wood and glaze; 40–60 GU on aged brass
finish.patina: The style wants a surface that wears in well: brass darkens, oak takes a soft tone, linen softens, and a worn edge is a good sign.

hardware.section: Rods and handles 12–22 mm; a tap body 30–45 mm
hardware.joints: Dovetails, pegs and through tenons in view on solid wood; plain screws on the back only.
hardware.handles: A turned oak knob, a leather loop or a brass bar of round section.
hardware.switches_and_taps: A small oak or brass toggle on a wood block; a knurled brass tap on a wall-mounted spout.

palette.strategy: Oat, sand, clay and bone, with soft black and aged brass as the only dark notes.

processes: wheel throwing and hand glazing of stoneware
hand weaving and garment washing of linen
manufacture.scale: A workshop of 1 to 10 makers, with batches of 1 to 100 pieces, or a small studio with named craft partners.
manufacture.signs: Throwing rings and a glaze that pools in the base, a plane mark on oak, a hand-set peg, and a maker mark on the foot.

objects.form: surface switch on a wood block
ginger-jar base with a drum shade
low long credenza on tapered legs
slab top on a trestle base

positive: studio product photograph, soft window light

evidence.title: Vas nr 20, glazed stoneware vase by Curt-M. Addin 1

emotion.target_response: Slow calm: the viewer wants to touch a warm surface that shows the hand and the time of its maker.

use_cases: a calm home or hotel moodboard
a product brief for a craft collection
a styled shelf or table for a still life
material schedules for a quiet interior
avoid_when: The brief asks for gloss, colour or plastic.
The room needs a machine-precise, technical look.

modifiers.how: Swap stoneware and oak for matte plastic and ash, and remove the marks of the hand.
Use pale birch, white glaze and slim tapered legs.
Use painted pine, peg rails and simple turned knobs.

era_blend.note: A new object in this style is the norm; a reissue of a craft original is the faithful case.
